```{r}
if (dir.exists('.Rlib')) .libPaths(c(normalizePath('.Rlib'), .libPaths()))
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(crosstalk)
library(htmltools)
invisible(Sys.setlocale('LC_CTYPE', 'en_US.UTF-8'))
mode <- Sys.getenv('NBA_ANALYSIS_MODE', 'archive')
stopifnot(mode %in% c('demo', 'live', 'archive'))
path <- file.path('output', mode, 'analysis.rds')
if (!file.exists(path)) stop('No analysis for mode ', mode,
  '. In the project Terminal, run: Rscript scripts/run.R --', mode)
result <- readRDS(path)
if (is.null(result$uncertainty) || is.null(result$robustness) || is.null(result$prepared$recent))
  stop('Analysis was generated by older code. Rebuild it: Rscript scripts/run.R --', mode)
stopifnot(identical(result$mode, mode))
d <- result$prepared$analysis
cohort <- result$prepared$cohort
metrics <- result$models$metrics
uncertainty <- result$uncertainty
robustness <- result$robustness
source('R/visuals.R')
findings <- finding_plots(result)
agility_cases <- filter(robustness$comparisons, comparison == '+ Lane agility')
demo <- identical(mode, 'demo')
latest_start <- max(result$config$season_starts)
latest_season <- sprintf('%d-%02d', latest_start, (latest_start + 1) %% 100)
latest_windows <- result$prepared$windows |>
  filter(season_start == latest_start, player_id %in% d$player_id)
label <- function(text) paste0(if (demo) 'SIMULATED · ' else '', text)
palette <- c(G = '#087f78', F = '#ce7231', C = '#5b66a5', Other = '#777777')
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
interactive_plot <- function(p) ggplotly(p) |> config(displaylogo = FALSE)
banner <- function() {
  if (demo) div(class = 'mode-banner', strong('SIMULATED PREVIEW — NO NBA FINDINGS'),
    tags$br(), 'All players and results on this page are invented to test the software. ',
    'Do not interpret model scores or chart patterns as evidence about basketball.')
  else div(class = 'research-note', strong('OBSERVATIONAL NBA ANALYSIS'), tags$br(),
    'Shot-defense associations among measured combine participants with matched NBA outcomes. ',
    'This is not a causal estimate or an overall defensive ranking. ',
    if (mode == 'archive') 'Data: original NBA responses archived by SportsDataverse. ' else '',
    paste0('Latest included season: ', latest_season, '.'))
}
```

```{r}
banner()
tags$p('Does lane agility improve prediction of defended-shot outcomes beyond size and position? ',
       'Lower agility times are faster; lower defensive shooting gaps are better.')
tags$div(class = 'stat-grid',
  div(class = 'stat', strong(nrow(cohort)), span('Combine participants after deduplication')),
```

### Read the result {.height=auto}

```{r}
base <- metrics$rmse[metrics$model == 'Size + position']
agility <- metrics$rmse[metrics$model == '+ Lane agility']
delta <- base - agility
if (demo) {
  tags$p(strong('No research conclusion is available from simulated data.'))
} else {
  interval <- filter(uncertainty, comparison == '+ Lane agility')
  tagList(
    tags$p(sprintf('Adding lane agility %s held-out RMSE by %.4f percentage points.',
      if (delta >= 0) 'reduced' else 'increased', abs(delta))),
    tags$p(sprintf('The 95%% paired bootstrap interval for the RMSE improvement is %.4f to %.4f pp.',
      interval$rmse_lower, interval$rmse_upper)),
    tags$p('See Robustness for alternative class windows and shot thresholds. ',
           'Intervals are conditional on the fitted models; they do not include training or future-class variability.'))
}
tags$p('Training classes: ', paste(result$models$train_years, collapse = ', '),
       '. Held-out test classes: ', paste(result$models$test_years, collapse = ', '), '.')
tags$p('Classes omitted between training and test to prevent overlapping outcome windows: ',
       paste(result$models$embargo_years, collapse = ', '), '.')
knitr::kable(metrics, digits = 2, col.names = c('Model', 'Players', 'RMSE (pp)', 'MAE (pp)'))
```

## Row {height="auto"}

### Reading the early results {.height=auto}

The 2024 class can contribute 2024–25 and 2025–26; the 2025 class can contribute 2025–26.
These unequal follow-up periods should not be compared as if they were complete three-season outcomes.
Players need both plotted measurements to appear as dots; a missing dot is not a zero result.
The early-outcome chart includes small shot samples, which can fluctuate substantially. Hover to check attempts.
Select a player above to focus on their available measurements. Full player-level exports, including missing results,
are in `output/<mode>/recent.csv`.

## Row

### Adjusted response

```{r}
interactive_plot(ggplot(result$models$effects, aes(lane_agility_time, predicted_gap)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3, color = '#0d776f') +
  labs(title = label('Model response to lane agility'), x = 'Lane agility (seconds)',
       y = 'Average predicted defense gap (pp)',
       subtitle = 'Training-player profiles held fixed; 5th–95th percentile range'))
```

### Predicted versus observed

```{r}
pred <- filter(result$models$predictions, model == '+ Lane agility')
interactive_plot(ggplot(pred, aes(defense_gap_pp, predicted,
  text = paste0(player_name, '<br>Combine: ', combine_year))) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = '#888') +
  geom_point(color = '#0d776f', alpha = .7) +
  labs(title = label('Held-out test players'), x = 'Observed defense gap (pp)', y = 'Predicted gap (pp)'))
```

## Row

### What this model tests {.height=auto}

The same eligible players are used for every model. Ridge regression shrinks correlated measurements and provides an interpretable first benchmark. The **size + position** model includes height, wingspan, weight, position, and combine year. We then add lane agility; the full model adds the remaining drills.

Penalty strength is selected by rolling forward through training draft classes. Both inner validation and final testing omit classes whose three-season outcome window would not have finished before the prediction combine. Every validation fold learns its own imputation and scaling from earlier, fully observed classes. The latest configured classes are held out until final evaluation. Scores weight each player equally; defended-shot volume controls eligibility rather than silently allowing high-volume players to dominate the prediction target.

The adjusted response curve changes agility while holding the other training-player features fixed. It is a model diagnostic, not a causal effect, a confidence interval, or evidence that training a faster drill improves defense.

```{r}

```

# Robustness

## Row {height="auto"}

### How certain is the apparent improvement? {.height=auto}

```{r}
#| height: auto
banner()
tags$p('Positive differences mean lower error than size + position; negative differences mean higher error. ',
       'Intervals are 95% paired percentile bootstrap intervals from ', result$config$bootstrap_reps,
       ' resamples of held-out players within each draft class.')
if (!demo) tags$p(sprintf('Agility lowers RMSE in %d of %d evaluated scenarios. These overlapping scenarios are not independent replications.',
  sum(agility_cases$delta_rmse > 0), nrow(agility_cases)))
```

## Row {height="320px"}

### Primary held-out comparison

```{r}
#| height: 320px
interactive_plot(ggplot(uncertainty, aes(x = delta_rmse, y = comparison)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = '#777') +
  geom_segment(aes(x = rmse_lower, xend = rmse_upper, yend = comparison), linewidth = 1, color = '#0d776f') +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = '#ce7231') +
  labs(title = label('RMSE improvement and uncertainty'), x = 'Size + position RMSE minus comparison RMSE (pp)',
       y = NULL))
```

## Row {height="550px"}

### Results depend on classes and shot thresholds

```{r}
#| height: 550px
case_plot <- agility_cases |> mutate(window = ifelse(test_start == test_end,
  as.character(test_start), paste0(test_start, '–', test_end)),
  threshold = factor(threshold))
interactive_plot(ggplot(case_plot, aes(x = delta_rmse, y = window,
  text = paste0('Shots ≥ ', threshold, '<br>Test players: ', players,
                '<br>RMSE improvement: ', round(delta_rmse, 4), ' pp'))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = '#777') +
  geom_segment(aes(x = rmse_lower, xend = rmse_upper, yend = window), color = '#0d776f') +
  geom_point(color = '#ce7231', size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~threshold, ncol = 2, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(title = label('Added lane agility: sensitivity'), x = 'RMSE improvement (pp; positive is better)',
       y = NULL))
```

## Row {height="auto"}

### What the intervals cover {.height=auto}

Both models are evaluated on the same players in each resample. Resampling preserves each draft class's sample size and all model predictions for a selected player. The intervals describe test-player sampling uncertainty **conditional on the fitted models and observed draft classes**. They do not include model refitting, uncertainty in shot-level outcomes, or variation across future classes and team environments.

Each scenario independently retunes its ridge penalty using earlier training classes, with the three-season outcome gap enforced in both tuning and evaluation. Lower shot thresholds can restore players excluded by the primary cutoff. Test windows overlap and their samples change with the cutoff, so the scenarios cannot be pooled as independent experiments. These are exploratory, pointwise intervals without adjustment for multiple comparisons; one interval excluding zero does not establish a repeatable scouting advantage.

### Scenario coverage {.height=auto}

```{r}
#| height: auto
tags$p(nrow(robustness$splits), ' of ', robustness$planned_cases, ' planned scenarios were evaluated.')
if (nrow(robustness$skipped)) {
  knitr::kable(robustness$skipped)
} else {
  tags$p('No scenarios were skipped.')
}
knitr::kable(select(agility_cases, threshold, test_start, test_end, train_players, players,
                    delta_rmse, rmse_lower, rmse_upper), digits = 4)
```

## Row

### Outcome and interpretation {.height=auto}

**Defense gap (percentage points)** = 100 × [total defended makes / total defended attempts − the attempt-weighted normal opponent FG%]. Negative means opponents shot below their usual percentage on the recorded defended attempts. Season summaries are weighted by defended attempts, not averaged equally.

This endpoint does not directly measure defensive slides, isolation containment, screen navigation, or overall defensive impact. We begin with recorded **lane agility** and retain modified lane agility as a separate measurement. Verify the drill definitions before calling either a defensive-slide test.

Participation and missing drill results can select an unusual subset of prospects. No matched NBA observation does not mean a prospect was a poor defender or never played in the NBA. Team schemes, opponent quality, assignments, injuries, and playing opportunity can influence outcomes. This first version adjusts for combine size and position, and does not claim to account for those other factors.
